item.text:
## 1B.1 Research Note: Lula, Brazil, 2024

Net assessment: **mostly yes**. In 2024, the strongest available evidence shows Lula taking repeated de-escalatory, multilateral, and disarmament-oriented positions, including direct support for dialogue, ceasefires, and a formal disarmament delegation. I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence that he sought nuclear leverage or escalation for prestige/power. The main counterevidence is rhetorical escalation in the Gaza case, which increased diplomatic tension but was still paired with ceasefire and two-state language.

### Accepted claims

- **Claim:** Lula’s government formally re-established Brazil’s permanent presence in the UN Conference on Disarmament, a direct institutional step aligned with nuclear-risk reduction.
  - **Title:** Decreto nº 12.237, de 25 de outubro de 2024
  - **Publisher:** Presidência da República / Planalto
  - **Date:** October 25, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2023-2026/2024/Decreto/D12237.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** The decree created Brazil’s permanent delegation to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva. That is direct evidence of support for disarmament diplomacy rather than escalation.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.1`

- **Claim:** Lula publicly framed Brazil’s position on Ukraine and Gaza as one of peace and negotiation.
  - **Title:** Lula diz que discutiu conflitos em Gaza e na Ucrânia em encontro com Blinken
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** February 21, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/21/lula-diz-que-discutiu-conflitos-em-gaza-e-na-ucrania-em-encontro-com-blinken.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula said he discussed peace in Ukraine and Gaza with Antony Blinken; the Planalto separately said Lula reaffirmed his desire for peace and an end to the conflicts, including support for a Palestinian state. This supports a de-escalatory intent.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.1`

- **Claim:** Brazil and China advanced a joint peace initiative for Ukraine built around dialogue and a ceasefire.
  - **Title:** Brasil e China assinam proposta conjunta de negociação de paz para guerra da Ucrânia e Rússia
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** May 23, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/05/23/brasil-e-china-assinam-proposta-conjunta-de-negociacao-de-paz-para-guerra-da-ucrania-e-russia.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** The joint statement said dialogue and negotiation were the only viable solution and called for conditions to resume direct talks and move toward a comprehensive ceasefire. That is clear evidence of risk-reduction behavior.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.1`

- **Claim:** At the UN General Assembly, Lula explicitly criticized rising military spending and nuclear arsenals and called for dialogue, ceasefire, and less militarized global governance.
  - **Title:** Speech by President Lula at the opening of the 79th UN General Assembly in New York
  - **Publisher:** Brazil G20 / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
  - **Date:** September 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/g20/en/documents/speeches/speech-by-president-lula-at-the-opening-of-the-79th-un-general-assembly-in-new-york
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula said global military spending and nuclear arsenals were rising, that destructive weapons were taking the world toward Cold War-style confrontation, and that direct dialogue was crucial. He also argued AI should be “a tool for peace, not war.” This is strong evidence for reducing existential risk.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.1`

- **Claim:** Lula’s Gaza rhetoric in February 2024 was highly escalatory in diplomatic terms, even though he still coupled it with anti-war language.
  - **Title:** Lula repete que governo israelense comete genocídio em Gaza e defende criação de Estado palestino
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** February 23, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/23/lula-repete-que-governo-israelense-comete-genocidio-em-gaza-e-defende-criacao-de-estado-palestino.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula repeated the “genocide” accusation, defended Palestinian statehood, and reaffirmed opposition to war generally. The article reports a major diplomatic rupture with Israel. This is the main counterevidence: it shows confrontational rhetoric that increased tension, though not evidence of nuclear brinkmanship or power-seeking escalation.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.1`

- **Claim:** Lula’s government also took 2024 climate-risk actions that fit “other existential risk” reduction.
  - **Title:** Lula anuncia criação de Autoridade Climática
  - **Publisher:** Brazil Ministry of Environment and Climate Change
  - **Date:** September 10, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/lula-anuncia-criacao-de-autoridade-climatica
  - **Claim-level summary:** The ministry said Lula announced a Climate Authority and a technical-scientific committee to improve responses to extreme climate events. This does not speak to nuclear policy, but it is relevant to reducing catastrophic climate risk.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.1`

### Search gap

I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence that Lula pursued nuclear escalation, nuclear signaling, or any explicit increase in existential risk for leverage, prestige, or personal power. The 2024 record I found is dominated by:
- disarmament institution-building,
- ceasefire and negotiation advocacy,
- UN-level calls against militarization,
- and climate-risk governance.
